claims.text: The starting material is a single-phase solid-solution high-entropy alloy in which titanium and nickel are primary constituents.
A post-fabrication aging treatment at approximately 650–800 °C will activate nanoscale precipitation in the alloy.
The aging treatment will produce uniformly distributed nanoscale precipitates.
The aging-induced nanoprecipitates will be coherent with the alloy matrix.
The nanoprecipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
The nanoprecipitates will obstruct grain-boundary sliding.
Obstruction of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will increase high-temperature yield strength.
Obstruction of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will reduce the high-temperature creep rate.
The aged alloy will have greater yield strength than the unaged alloy under elevated-temperature testing.
The aged alloy will have greater ultimate tensile strength than the unaged alloy under elevated-temperature testing.
The aged alloy will have better creep resistance than the unaged alloy under elevated-temperature testing.
The beneficial effect is expected in elevated-temperature test regimes of approximately 600–800 °C under moderate aging conditions.
Excessively high aging temperatures or prolonged aging may coarsen the precipitates.
Precipitate coarsening may diminish the strengthening effect.
